 Smallest Font 
 Largest Font 
 Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George has continued competing despite a sprained right ankle sustained against the Minnesota Timberwolves on November 8, 2026. The injury has affected his performance during a difficult stretch for Utah, which is dealing with multiple absences and a 12-game losing streak.
 According to reports from KSL Sports journalist Ben Anderson, George returned after missing just one game, although his ankle had not fully recovered. The fourth-year guard has struggled to reproduce his earlier offensive production while continuing to play.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 Anderson described George's condition as "playing hurt." The journalist also observed that the injured ankle appeared "twice the size" of his left ankle when George sat in the locker room following Utah's loss to the San Antonio Spurs.

 George's physical condition has coincided with a noticeable decline in his scoring efficiency. According to statistics reported by Sports Illustrated, he averaged 17.7 points per game while shooting 33 percent from the field across his three appearances following the injury.
 Before suffering the ankle sprain, George had averaged 21.1 points per game through 10 appearances, connecting on 45 percent of his field-goal attempts. The difference highlights the decline in his offensive production since returning to the lineup.
 Anderson also documented George's response when asked about his condition in the locker room. Despite the visible swelling, the guard declined to make his injury an excuse for his performances.

 "Watching from the locker room, the reason for his struggles wasn’t difficult to spot. Beneath the chair where George sat hunched over, his injured right ankle is twice the size of his left. Still, he offered no excuses. 'It’s fine,' he tells me. 'I’m straight."
 The injury situation adds to Utah's broader roster problems during its difficult start to the 2026-27 NBA season. Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr., Jusuf Nurkic and Jaxson Hayes have also missed time because of injuries, according to Sports Illustrated.
 Utah's record stood at 1-13 in the early-season stretch covered by the November 17 report. The team had regularly been without three or four important players, making consistent lineup availability a continuing challenge.

 Sports Illustrated reported that Markkanen and Jackson were trending toward December returns rather than coming back within the following couple of weeks. Their absences leave coach Will Hardy relying on the available roster to maintain competitiveness.
 Among the players expected to help Utah manage the situation are Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. George remains an important offensive contributor despite the ankle problem, while the Jazz continue waiting for injured players to return.
